title: Chicken Parmigiana
subtitle: Breaded chicken baked with tomato sauce and melted mozzarella
excerpt: The panko crust gives more crunch than fine breadcrumbs, and the quick pan-fry before the oven means the coating stays crisp even under the tomato sauce and cheese. Do not skip the oven stage -- it is what melts the mozzarella into the chicken properly.
sourceNotes: Chicken parmigiana is an Italian-American adaptation of the Sicilian melanzane alla parmigiana, which uses aubergine rather than chicken. It became one of the defining dishes of Italian-American red-sauce restaurants and now appears across pub menus and home kitchens worldwide.

content.text: Dry the chicken well before flouring -- moisture under the crumb coating leads to steaming rather than crisping. Press the breadcrumbs on firmly with your palm.

Heat the oven to 200 C. Flatten the chicken breasts to about 1 cm. Set up three shallow bowls: one with flour seasoned with salt and pepper, one with beaten egg, and one with the panko breadcrumbs mixed with half the grated parmesan.
For the tomato sauce, soften the garlic in 1 tbsp of olive oil over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, oregano, and a pinch of sugar. Simmer for 10 minutes and season.
Coat each chicken breast in flour, then egg, then press firmly into the breadcrumb mixture on both sides.
Heat the remaining olive oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the crumbed chicken for 2-3 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to the baking tray.
Spoon a few tablespoons of tomato sauce over each piece of chicken. Top with torn mozzarella and the remaining parmesan.
Bake for 15-18 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the chicken is cooked through. Scatter with basil leaves and serve.

items.symptom: Crumb coating falling off during frying.
items.cause: Not pressing the breadcrumbs on firmly enough, or oil not hot enough.
items.fix: Press each coated piece firmly and let the oil heat for a full minute before the chicken goes in.
Pat the mozzarella dry with paper towel before using, or opt for a drier block mozzarella.
